newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money unchanged, repo drain seen.
newsitem.headline: German call money unchanged, repo drain seen.

text.p: German call money rates were unchanged at 3.10/3.12 percent on Tuesday as the market remained adequately furnished with liquidity.
Dealers predicted the Bundesbank will allocate about 60 billion marks at its weekly repo allotment on Wednesday, nine billion marks less than the volume of repos expiring this week.
The drain would give room for the Bundesbank's 1996 profit which flows into the money market on Thursday and is expected to total slightly less than 10 billion marks.

Dealers saw a chance that the call money rate may ease to 3.05 percent at the end of the week but added that given the dollar's strength against the mark, there was virtually no market speculation of an interest rate cut at Thursday's Bundesbank meeting.

Commercial banks' effective deposits at the Bundesbank on Monday slipped to 39.8 billion marks from 40.1 billion and the average for the month through Monday was 41.0 billion marks, down from 41.1 billion.
Borrowing from the Bundesbank's Lombard facility was negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) was 3.13033 percent on Tuesday compared with 3.13567 percent on Monday.
